headline: Revenue climbs as higher interest costs squeeze earnings
summary_short: SBA Communications grew Q2 2026 revenue 2.3% y/y to $715.3M, but diluted EPS fell 10.7% to $1.87 and AFFO per share fell 3.8% to $3.05 as net cash interest expense rose 9.5% following new debt issuance.
summary_long: International site leasing led growth, with segment revenue up 30.5% y/y and operating profit up 31.9%, while domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.7% on Sprint and EchoStar consolidation churn. Net cash interest expense rose 9.5% y/y as SBA issued $3.5B of new investment-grade senior notes in July to refinance secured debt, pressuring net income and AFFO despite operating income growth. SBA raised its FY2026 revenue and AFFO outlook slightly while trimming Adjusted EBITDA and Tower Cash Flow guidance by $1M each. The board declared a $1.25/share quarterly dividend. Cash stood at $327.1M against $12.8B total debt, with net leverage at 6.4x, mid-range of the 6.0x-7.0x target.

drivers.explanation: International site leasing revenue rose 30.5% y/y on new colocations and tower builds (notably for Millicom in Central America); domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.7% y/y on Sprint and EchoStar consolidation churn.
Net cash interest expense rose 9.5% y/y ahead of July's note offering, and the prior-year quarter had a larger $30.4M FX remeasurement gain on intercompany loans vs $8.0M this quarter.
Higher interest expense and a smaller currency-remeasurement gain ($8.0M vs $30.4M a year ago) outweighed operating income growth and lower asset-impairment costs.
Site leasing segment operating profit rose 3.2% y/y (international +31.9%, domestic -4.8%), while asset impairment and decommission costs fell to $22.6M from $45.2M a year ago.
Growth was essentially flat on a constant-currency basis (0.0% ex-FX per the company's own reconciliation), meaning the y/y gain is mostly a currency effect rather than underlying expansion.

A $10.6M y/y rise in net cash interest expense outpaced revenue and Adjusted EBITDA growth; the release also flags $2.8M of nonrecurring tax tied to the sale of the company's Canadian operations affecting AFFO comparability.
Operating cash flow rose to $407.2M from $368.1M a year ago, while investing outflows were far smaller than the prior-year quarter's larger acquisition spend.

Debt is modestly higher y/y ahead of July's $3.5B unsecured notes issuance (post-quarter-end) used to refinance secured debt and the revolver; within the quarter itself, changes were limited to normal revolver activity.

Management called the quarter 'in line with expectations,' with the balance-sheet story — an inaugural $3.5B investment-grade bond, a new $2.5B unsecured revolver, and an S&P upgrade to BBB — overshadowing the operating results.
